prompt_text: I am planning a trip. Should I book on Airbnb, Vrbo, or Booking.com, and how do I find a good host?
answer_verbatim:
Short answer: check all three and choose the listing that best matches your priorities (type of place, price after fees, cancellation policy, trust in host). Below is a quick comparison to help you decide, followed by practical steps and a checklist for finding a good host.

Which platform when
- Airbnb — Best for variety and unique stays (private rooms, entire homes, treehouses, experiences). Good if you want host interaction or unusual places. Has built-in guest protections (AirCover) and widely used reviews/Superhost program.
- Vrbo — Best for whole-home vacation rentals (families/groups, multi-bedroom houses). Listings tend to be whole properties rather than shared rooms, and many owners are professional vacation-rental managers.
- Booking.com — Best for instant-book hotels and many apartments; strong for last-minute bookings, flexible cancellation options, and easy comparisons with hotels. Many short-term rentals are listed here too, often with instant confirmation.

How to choose between them
1. Compare the same property across sites (often listed on multiple platforms). Compare total price (cleaning, service fees, taxes) and cancellation terms.
2. Pick by what you value most: unique/hosted experience (Airbnb), family-sized whole homes (Vrbo), or instant booking/hotel-like reliability (Booking.com).
3. Consider platform support: Booking.com and Airbnb usually have quicker customer-service channels; Airbnb emphasizes guest protections.

How to find a good host — step-by-step
1. Read recent reviews (last 6–12 months) — focus on cleanliness, accuracy of listing, check-in, responsiveness, and neighborhood.
2. Look for “Superhost” (Airbnb) / “Premier host” or high owner ratings (Vrbo) / high property rating and many reviews (Booking.com). These are helpful but not foolproof.
3. Check response rate & response time on the host’s profile and see if they answer questions in reviews. A responsive host reduces stress.
4. Inspect photos + description carefully — match amenities, number of beds, exact sleeping arrangements, and check-in process.
5. Verify policies: cancellation, house rules, pets, extra guest fees, security deposit, and check-in/out times.
6. Confirm logistics: parking, elevator, stairs, noise level, proximity to transit, and wifi speed (ask for Mbps if you need it).
7. Message the host before booking with specific questions (see sample below). Gauge clarity and timeliness of replies.
8. Watch for red flags: no reviews, few/low-quality photos, host asking to pay off-platform, inconsistent calendar or last-minute huge price drops, evasive answers.
9. Keep all booking/payment on the platform. Save screenshots of the listing, messages, and receipts after booking.
10. Check cancellation/refund and dispute policies in advance and understand how to contact platform support.

Practical checklist before you click “book”
- Total price after all fees and taxes looks acceptable.
- Recent guest reviews confirm accuracy and cleanliness.
- Host has a good rating and responds quickly to messages.
- Cancellation policy is acceptable for your needs.
- You know exact check-in instructions, parking, access code or key handoff.
- The platform shows verified identity or host verification if available.
- There is no request to communicate or pay outside the platform.

Sample pre-booking message to a host
Hi — I’m [name], traveling with [number and relation, e.g., “2 adults, 1 child”]. Your place looks great. A few quick questions: 
1) Is the bedroom setup/sofa bed as pictured?  
2) How is parking and late check-in handled?  
3) What’s the typical wifi speed?  
4) Any building or neighborhood restrictions we should know about?  
Thanks — we plan to book if the answers match the listing.

After booking
- Confirm arrival instructions and any last-minute needs.
- Note the host’s contact details and platform dispute contact.
- Take photos of the place on arrival for your record.

If you tell me your travel dates, destination, group size, and priorities (price, unique stay, kids, work-from-anywhere, last-minute), I can recommend the best platform and help draft messages or shortlist features to filter for.
